provenance: cold-reviewer finding 1 (M2 close-out): normalize() formatted numbers with '%g', which is 6 significant digits, so the grader declared $12,345.67 and $12,345.74 equal — and every price above ~$9,999 lost its cents at the one layer whose entire job is deciding whether an answer is right. No golden case had an answer longer than 4 significant digits, so the numeric branch was only ever exercised where it happened to be exact. Tagged invariant: a grader that cannot tell two numbers apart invalidates every other measurement in the repo.
